rubrics.justification: Describes a high-quality expanded/full blastocyst with compact ICM, cohesive TE, and thinned zona consistent with the provided Gardner details; appropriately notes possible 3 vs 4 stage nomenclature uncertainty. Slight limitation because some image-specific claims cannot be fully verified from a single static view.

Thoroughly integrates maternal age, ovarian reserve, tubal factor, prior live birth, endometrial thickness, partner age, semen parameters, and lifestyle with embryo quality and prognosis, including the important hydrosalpinx caveat.

Reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong morphology plus favorable patient factors leads to above-average prognosis, while acknowledging uncertainty from untested status and tubal disease details. Probability estimate is well supported.

Recommendations are well aligned with IVF practice standards: elective single embryo transfer in a young good-prognosis patient, caution about untreated hydrosalpinx, avoidance of unsupported add-ons, and nuanced discussion of PGT-A.

Provides clear practical next steps for transfer and contingency planning, including SET, hydrosalpinx evaluation, standard luteal support, and when to consider further testing. Slightly less specific on transfer protocol details, so not maximal.
